newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand aims to boost commodity sales to China.
newsitem.headline: Thailand aims to boost commodity sales to China.

text.p: Thailand will secure deals to sell more rice, rubber and tapioca to China when Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh visits Bejing from April 2-5, a senior commerce ministry official said on Monday.

Orajit Singkalvanich, deputy director general of the foreign trade department, told Reuters that Thailand had targeted sales of 700,000 tonnes of rice, 400,000 tonnes of rubber and 100,000 tonnes of tapioca starch to China this year.

She said Thai delegates would inform their Chinese counterparts during Chavalit's visit of their targeted sales amounts but the quantities would not be specified in a final memorandum of understanding that would be signed.
"China was receptive to the proposal but said it prefers that the specific amount not be mentioned in the memorandum as other countries might want to do the same in the future," she said.
"But at least, the memorandum will say that China will buy more of the mentioned commodities from Thailand this year than last year."
China imported 630,000 tonnes of rice, 350,000 tonnes of rubber and 40,000-50,000 tonnes of tapioca starch from Thailand in 1996.
Thailand would also seek to increase the sale of fruit and vegetables to the country during the visit, Orajit said.
She added Thailand would ask China to buy more lower quality rice as it generally bought top grades, especially the expensive fragrant grade from Thailand.
"Of the 700,000 tonnes we propose to sell, we want China to buy about 200,000 tonnes of 10-25 percent grade," Orajit said.
Higher Thai rice prices have alienated countries which buy lower quality grades, and they have increasingly turned to cheaper producers such as Vietnam and Pakistan.
To facilitate trade between the two countries, Thailand will request that China relax its trade tariffs and regulations.
In return, Thailand would buy steel and chemical fertiliser from China, Orajit said.
